content.scenario: You are leading a team project. One team member consistently misses deadlines without valid reasons. The project deadline is approaching fast.
content.bestWorstQuestion: Choose the BEST and WORST approaches from the following:
responseOptions: A. Privately discuss the situation and set clear expectations with the team member
B. Report the issue immediately to senior management
C. Ignore the problem and hope the team member improves
D. Criticize the team member publicly in the next team meeting
E. Take over the team member's work yourself

content.scenario: Your team is facing a technical challenge that none of you have encountered before. You have a tight deadline.
content.bestWorstQuestion: Select the BEST and WORST courses of action:
responseOptions: A. Research solutions online and consult colleagues
B. Ask for a deadline extension immediately
C. Panic and blame others for the situation
D. Experiment with unknown solutions without backup plans
E. Consult with experienced experts outside the team

content.scenario: You need to give critical feedback to a skilled employee who is performing well overall but has one bad habit that affects the team.
content.bestWorstQuestion: Choose the most effective and least effective approaches:
responseOptions: A. Schedule a private meeting focused on specific behaviors
B. Provide feedback in an email to avoid discomfort
C. Bring it up casually in team meetings
D. Wait for someone else to address it
E. Point out the issue immediately in front of others

content.scenario: You discover that a colleague has been taking shortcuts that could compromise product quality, but they are your friend.
content.bestWorstQuestion: Select the most and least appropriate actions:
responseOptions: A. Report the issue to management anonymously
B. Talk to your friend privately about concerns first
C. Keep quiet because they are your friend
D. Confront them publicly to discourage others
E. Report it directly to management with evidence

content.scenario: During a high-pressure deadline, two team members start arguing about technical approach, potentially delaying the project.
content.bestWorstQuestion: Choose the best and worst ways to handle this:
responseOptions: A. Listen to both sides and facilitate a compromise
B. Step aside and let them resolve it on their own
C. Take sides immediately based on your expertise
D. Send everyone home to cool off
E. Call an immediate meeting with all stakeholders
